rust.summary:
P1b is done and every settle command passes. That includes the openpyxl exchange in both directions, which now also shows a bold font and a percent format written by openpyxl surviving a read-edit-save through this crate. The "save back to the same file, then a corrupt deflate stream" hazard is reproduced and fixed. With adopt removed from `write_into`, `a_saved_workbook_reopens_in_place` fails with "corrupt deflate stream"; with it, it passes. `a_failed_write_leaves_the_workbook_dirty` fails if the save is marked before the write.

**Dirty tracking and saving (`workbook.rs`)**
- `Slot` now carries `name`, `key`, `sheet_id`, `kind`, `state`, `part`, `parsed` and `saved`, with the dirty rule exactly as the design writes it. A sheet that was only read or parsed counts as clean.
- New public items:
  - `SheetKey`, with `as_u32`.
  - On `Workbook`: `sheet_key`, `sheet_by_key`, `is_dirty`, `parse_all`, `into_package`, `rebase`, `write_into` and `style_sheet`.
  - `Package`, with `as_bytes` and `into_bytes`.
- `into_bytes` now goes through `into_package` and leaves the workbook's state unchanged.
- `write_into` builds the package, adopts it as the workbook's source, writes the target once, and only then counts the workbook as saved. `rebase` does adopt plus mark, and refuses another workbook's package with `Error::Conflict`.
- `sheetId` is kept, and an added sheet takes the highest id the workbook has ever had plus one. Existing relationship ids are kept too.
- There is now one writer, `write_preserving`, over `Source::Archive` or `Source::Template` (the four template documents are constants in `package.rs`).
  - It writes exactly the dirty sheets and copies every other member with `copy_member_from`, never inflating it.
  - On any save that wrote a sheet or changed the sheet list, it sets or inserts `calcPr fullCalcOnLoad="1"` at its schema position, and removes `xl/calcChain.xml` together with its relationship and its content-type `Override`.
  - It creates the shared strings only when a written sheet adds a string, and the styles only when a sheet is written and the package has none.
- Deleted: `write_fresh`, `write_workbook`, `write_content_types`, `write_workbook_relationships`, `write_root_relationships`, `set_attribute` and `WrittenStyles`.

**`package::rewrite`**
- Gained the `attributes` hook (set or remove) and the `insert` hook (a fragment placed before the first present sibling in schema order), plus `Default`.
- `RelationshipKind` gained its 11 new variants.
- `relationships_part_of`, `folder_of`, `relative_to` (now producing `..` targets) and `escape_attribute` moved into `package.rs`.

**Styles (`styles.rs`, `style.rs`)**
- `StyleSheet` reads every fact listed in design §3.2 and carries the other lists untouched. Its public surface is `style`, `len`, `is_empty` and `indexed_colors`, plus the constant `MAX_CELL_FORMATS`.
- The crate-side `intern` deduplicates by content and refuses past 64,000 entries. A new number-format id is `max(163, declared) + 1`, and only built-in table ids the part has not redeclared are reused.
- The writer is an append-only splice that patches the counts.
- `TemporalStyles` is interned on demand through `Splice`, and the record path's `Replaced` now hands the stream `&TemporalStyles`.
- New public value types in `style.rs`: `CellStyle`, `Font`, `Fill`, `Border`, `Edge`, `Alignment`, `Protection` and `Color`, plus the seven vocabulary enums (`Underline`, `VerticalRun`, `FontScheme`, `Horizontal`, `Vertical`, `BorderStyle`, `PatternType`).
- `Styles`, `NumberFormat::style_index` and the cellXfs-ordered `ALL` are gone.

**Sheets from another workbook (`sheet.rs`)**
- `Sheet` tracks its origin workbook. Inserted into a different workbook, it resets every `StyleId` and drops `cm`/`vm`, keeping values and number formats.
- A temporal cell whose style does not read as its format is written under the interned temporal style.
- A style id the workbook's styles do not hold is refused at save, naming the cell.

**Tests and benchmarks**
- 21 new tests plus rewritten pins across `excel/{workbook,styles,style,package,sheet,parser,shared_strings,writer}`.
- A new `iobase_calls` workbook pin:
  - A clean save is 10 source reads for 9 members, all raw copies.
  - A save after one edit is 7 copies plus 2 document reads.
  - The target sees `write_all_bytes=1`, and `rebase` makes 0 calls.
- Benchmark rows: `copy/raw` and `copy/reencoded` in the holder zip bench, `workbook_save_clean` and `workbook_save_dirty` in the Excel bench.

deviations: `documents_dirty` and `styles_dirty` are counter pairs (`documents`/`documents_saved`, `styles_revision`/`styles_saved`) instead of bools. The design's rebase requirement - edits made during the service's lock-free write stay dirty - needs to tell a change made after the snapshot apart from one before it, which a bool cannot. `is_dirty` reads them.
The design's `text` hook for `package::rewrite` is not added; it is optional in P1b and P2 needs it.

A sheet put in place of another with `insert_sheet` gets a new `SheetKey` and a new part (`sheetN` past every existing number). The part it replaced, and that part's `.rels`, are dropped as orphans. Before, the new sheet was written into the old part name.

Sheet relationship ids are now stable: existing `r:id`s are kept and only new tabs get new ids. Before, every sheet relationship was renumbered whenever the sheet list changed. Four pins were rewritten for this.
A relationship target outside the workbook part's folder is now written relative with `..` (for example `../xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml`) instead of absolute `/xl/...`.

When shared strings and styles are created: the shared strings only when a written sheet adds a string (a fresh workbook holding no text has none), and the styles only when the package has none and a sheet is written from its cells. A workbook built from nothing therefore holds the template styles plus the temporal styles it interned on demand, not six fixed formats.

An `s` index that names no cell format of the file (including files with no styles part) now reads as `StyleId::DEFAULT`. A style id set by the caller that the workbook's styles do not hold is refused at save, naming the cell. P1a dropped it silently; its pin `a_style_index_the_written_styles_part_does_not_hold_is_not_written` is replaced by `a_style_index_the_workbook_does_not_hold_is_refused_at_save_naming_the_cell`.
`NumberFormat::ALL` is now in enum order: General, Date, Time, DateTime, DateTimeFraction, Duration.
`NumberFormat::code()` for Time is now `h:mm:ss`, built-in id 21, matching design §3.4. It used to say `hh:mm:ss` while writing id 21.

Public additions not listed in the design: `StyleSheet::is_empty`, `StyleSheet::indexed_colors` (the palette design §3.2 asks to parse), the constant `excel::MAX_CELL_FORMATS`, `Debug` for `Package`, and `ALL`/`as_str`/`from_attribute`/`Display` on the seven style vocabularies.

Display codes for number-format ids a file does not declare: ECMA table ids get their en-US codes, ids 41-44 the en-US accounting codes, East Asian locale ids (27-36, 50-58) the en-US code of their kind, and any other id `General`. Ids 5-8 count as built-ins, because the design writes the table as 0-22.
Adopt copies the package bytes once into an in-memory buffer, so memory briefly holds the package twice.

A save that changes nothing does not read the workbook's relationships or content types; they are copied as stored. A save that writes a sheet reads the relationships once to learn whether a calculation chain is related.

Every test in `rust/tests/interop/excel.rs` takes the same mutex, so the new edit test (`edits_the_styled_workbook_...`) shares it. Its reading half prints `SKIPPED` on the first run, as the other reading halves do.
open: P3: `StyleSheet::intern` is reachable only through the temporal styles in this phase. The general path - fonts, fills, borders, and codes such as the 41-44 accounting formats that must be declared with a new id - is not pinned directly. Exposing it would need an `internals` module, and regenerating that edits `lib.rs`, which is outside this file set. P3's `set_style` should pin it.

P3: adopt resets the held styles table and re-reads it from the written package, which is safe only while nothing appends to the held table after the snapshot. Once `set_style` appends through `&mut self`, `rebase` must keep entries appended after the snapshot, and `styles_revision` must move with each such change (today nothing moves it).

P2: when a written sheet adds a string, the shared strings are still rewritten whole from `SharedStringTable`, so rich runs and phonetic text of existing items are lost and `count` counts only the rewritten sheets. When nothing is added, the part is copied as stored. `shared_strings.rs` is outside this file set.

P2: removing a sheet drops only its part and its `.rels`. Drawings, charts, tables and comments it referenced stay in the package unreferenced; the reference counting in design §2.7 is P2. Defined names, the `activeTab` remap and the `rich_package` fixture are also P2.

P2: the design's `an_edited_cell_changes_only_its_cell` needs `rich_package`. This phase adds `an_edited_cell_changes_only_its_sheet_and_the_documents_a_written_sheet_asks_for` over the existing fixtures instead.

- `.api-inventory.txt` needs `excel::{SheetKey, Package, StyleSheet, CellStyle, Font, Fill, Border, Edge, Alignment, Protection, Color, Underline, VerticalRun, FontScheme, Horizontal, Vertical, BorderStyle, PatternType, MAX_CELL_FORMATS}` and the `Workbook::{sheet_key, sheet_by_key, is_dirty, parse_all, into_package, rebase, write_into, style_sheet}` methods, and must drop `NumberFormat::style_index`.
- `docs/holder/index.md` still lacks the `copy_member_from` signature and cost line (the benchmark rows are added).

side.summary:
P2 UI for Agent B is done in cli/assets/excel/. Nothing was committed; no cargo, maturin or npm build was run, and no .rs file was touched.

**New modules**
- `js/editor.js` (`Editor`): the in-cell editor and the formula bar, both moved out of main.js along with the Name Box.
  - Typing replaces the cell; F2, a double click or a click in the formula bar edits the entry (fetched from `cells/{ref}`).
  - Enter, Tab and their Shift forms commit and move the way the grid's `walk` does. An arrow in Enter mode commits and moves, except inside a `=` formula.
  - Ctrl+Enter sends `fillEntry` over the selection and keeps it. Alt+Enter breaks the line, Esc cancels, Backspace clears and edits.
  - Ctrl+; and Ctrl+Shift+; type today and now in the workbook's timezone. Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo.
  - A refused entry (stale base, 400/413/422, or no answer) reopens on its cell with the typed text kept and the selection restored.
  - The Name Box goes through `resolve`.
- `js/ribbon.js` (`Ribbon`, `FORMATS`): every Home control, each as a command sending an op.
  - `setStyle` patches: font name and size, B/I/U/S, borders presets, fill and font colour, horizontal and vertical alignment, wrap, indent, number formats, the `$ % ,` buttons, decimals.
  - Other ops: merge and unmerge; insert and remove rows and columns; hide and unhide; add, remove and hide or unhide sheets; AutoSum; Fill down/right/up/left (`fill` with mode copy); Clear; Sort.
  - Pressed states and the pickers follow the active cell's style.
  - Keys: Ctrl+B/I/U/5, Delete, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+R, Alt+=, Shift+F11.
- `js/menus.js` (`Menus`, `colorItems`, `pasteItems`, `sortItems`, the colour swatches): one `role=menu` component with roving focus, submenus, typeahead, swatch grids and toggle-to-close.
  - Context menus for cells, row headers, column headers and sheet tabs; Shift+F10 and the ContextMenu key.
  - Ctrl+- and Ctrl+Shift+= act at once on whole rows or columns, and otherwise ask which.
  - An item whose command no phase has registered yet shows `aria-disabled`.

**Changes to P1 files**
- `main.js`: commands now take one options object (breaking for P3+ command code): `{element, value}` from a control, a menu item's `args` otherwise. `app.edit` hatches the target ranges, sends through `api.edit`, then applies the answer: styles, sheet list, tile invalidation, layout revalidation by ETag (`grid.setLayout`), catch-up through `changes?since=base`, and a debounced workbook refresh for the undo labels and dirty mark. It also adds a confirm `<dialog>` and title-bar Undo/Redo buttons.
- `api.js`: edits and history go one at a time, each carrying `base`; refusals carry `.base`; `adopt` never moves the revision backwards within a generation.
- `grid.js`: pending marks with `data-edits`, `setLayout`, and `activate`, `context` and `press` events.
- `render.js`: `fillText` inserts the fill at its `[char, offset]`; `paintPending` draws the hatch.
- `tiles.js`: `settled`, `hold`, `drop`. `selection.js`: `relayout`. `a11y.js`: `aria-busy` on pending cells, `setReadOnly`.
- `geometry.js`: `DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH` 9.140625.
- `index.html`: editable Name Box, one-row textarea formula bar, number-format option keys, confirm dialog. `styles.css` and `icons.svg` (undo, redo) updated to match.

**Contract decisions applied**
- `activeSheet` is read as a key.
- Widths are file `<col width>` units; the default is 9.140625, i.e. 64 px. Fixtures were regenerated with it.
- Tile `fill` is rendered as `[char, offset]`; Accounting pads after the `$`, and a new text fill cell pads after its text.

**Scratchpad**
- `dev.py` now sits on a new `devstore.py` that applies the ops to an in-memory store. It covers en-US entry, a small formula evaluator, number-format rendering with fill offsets and style interning. Revision, per-tile and layout ETags, the change ring and §8.6's stale-base 409 follow the contract, and a snapshot journal backs undo/redo. `POST /__control` adds edit latency for the tests.

deviations: §8.4 has no decimals op, and §3.4 puts FormatCode::with_decimals on the server, so the ±decimals buttons send `setStyle` with a new patch key `decimals: 1 | -1`. The dev server applies it per cell. This needs A's decision, or the patch table gains the key.

Built-in number formats go as their en-US codes, because the patch's numberFormat is a code: 14 m/d/yyyy, 19 h:mm:ss AM/PM, 10 0.00%, 12 # ?/?, 11 0.00E+00, 49 @, % button 0% (9). The service must intern them as the built-in ids. Accounting and Comma are sent as custom codes.
Where §8.4 is silent I assumed these spellings:
- at/start are 0-based, like layout runs;
- border presets are bottom, top, left, right, all, outside, thickOutside, none, with borders.style thin (thick for thickOutside) and color null for automatic;
- colours are #RRGGBB and null clears;
- underline is single or none; horizontal is general, left, center or right; vertical is top, center or bottom;
- sheetState takes hidden or visible; merge always sends center and across.
Undo and Redo are quick-access buttons in the title bar, which §10's ribbon table does not list. Undo while editing cancels the edit rather than committing and undoing it.
A minimal confirm dialog (app.confirm, the #confirm dialog) lives in main.js for Delete Sheet. dialogs.js (P3) should take it over.

Sort's header guess (text over non-text in the key column) and AutoSum's number trimming (edge bound plus the tiles' kind bits) run client-side. §8.4's sort requires header, and no endpoint answers either question.
Excel toggle rules are applied from the active cell's style:
- B/I/U/S and the alignment buttons toggle on the active cell;
- a pressed horizontal alignment returns to general, a pressed vertical one to bottom;
- increasing indent on a non-left/right cell also sends horizontal left;
- Merge & Center unmerges when the selection is exactly a merged cell.
In Enter mode, an arrow inside a formula moves the caret instead of committing, until point mode arrives in P5.
Keys for commands later phases register (Ctrl+1/F/H/G/S, F5, F9) do nothing and stay the browser's until those commands exist. Menu items for them show aria-disabled.

On stale_base the client reads changes?since=base&wait=0 to learn what to revalidate, because the problem carries only revision. It then adopts the revision. The editor reopens with the text; a ribbon op gets a toast and no automatic retry.
The formula bar is now a one-row textarea so Alt+Enter can break a line, and the Name Box is editable. The P1 check step 'ribbon: stubs do nothing' is renamed because the commands are now live.
open: Contract questions for A:
- the decimals patch key;
- 0-based at/start;
- the border, colour, underline and alignment spellings above;
- built-in codes interned to their ids;
- fillEntry carries no host cell. The dev server translates relative references from the first range's top-left, while Excel uses the active cell; fillEntry could carry the active cell as ref.

No long poll yet (sync.js is not in any phase list). Another tab's non-conflicting edits reach this tab only through its own next answer (catch-up when revision > base + 1), a 409, or ETag revalidation when a sheet is shown.

Not in P2: point mode, F4, token colours, autocomplete and the argument tip (P5); clipboard, Format Painter, Format Cells, row height and column width dialogs, status aggregates (P3); sheets.js rename, move and drag, and Find/Replace/Go To/Custom Sort (P4). The menus and keys for these already name their commands.
Not browser-tested: read-only mode (aria-readonly and the local refusal are implemented), IME composition into the editor, browsers other than Chromium.

A tile fetch in flight when a sheet is removed still gets a 404 from any server. tiles.hold and tiles.drop stop anything new being sent, and the check waits for the new sheet to load before undoing it.
dev.py still answers from fixtures; the switch to proxying the real binary is P9.

findings.issue: A styles part with no `cellXfs` entries (bare `<styleSheet>` with fonts/fills/borders only) breaks both write paths. VERIFIED with a probe built against the phase's rlib. (a) Workbook path: a dirty sheet is refused for a cell that states no `s`: `invalid record value at Sheet1!A1: expected a style the workbook's 0 cell formats hold, got index 0`, because `PartWriter::cell` (sheet.rs:1365) checks `own >= table.len()` even for `StyleId::DEFAULT`. This is a new refusal; P1a saved such a workbook. (b) Record path is silent corruption: `StyleSheet::intern` gives the first interned xf index `xfs.len() == 0`, i.e. the implicit default style. The interned date xf becomes style 0, so every cell written without `s` is a date. Probe: a Date32 column plus a Float64 column overwritten into such a package reads back with B2 (2.5) as `DateTime64(-2208859200000 ms)`, and the header text cells report `NumberFormat::Date`. Neither the model nor `intern` guarantees that xf 0 exists.
findings.fix: Make the model always hold the default xf at index 0. In `StyleSheet::intern`, when `self.xfs` is empty, first push the default `Xf` (with its resolved style and kind) so the interned id is at least 1. The splice then writes `<cellXfs count="N+1">` with the default first and `is_grown` reports it. In `PartWriter::cell` (sheet.rs:1365) only run the `table.len()` check when `own != StyleId::DEFAULT`. Add red-first tests in rust/tests/excel/styles.rs (styles part with no `cellXfs`): a dirty save succeeds and writes no `s` for default cells, and a record write of Date32 plus Float64 reads B2 back as a number under style 0.

findings.issue: `set_date_system` changes `date1904` in the workbook part (design 2.3 lists the date system under `documents_dirty`), but every worksheet that is not parsed is copied raw, because 'an unparsed slot is clean'. Its serials are then reinterpreted under the new system. VERIFIED: two sheets holding 45292 under a date xf; open, `set_date_system(Year1904)`, `into_bytes`, reopen. Sheet1 (parsed) keeps Date32 19723; Sheet2 (never parsed) reads Date32 21185, so its dates shift by 1462 days with no error. The doc on `set_date_system` says it counts serials 'in every sheet written'. The behaviour predates P1b (P1a carried unparsed sheets raw too), but this phase's dirty rule and `parse_all` are the place it must be settled. Simply making unparsed slots dirty does not fix it, because `parse()` reads under `self.system`, which is already the new system.
findings.fix: Change `pub fn set_date_system(&mut self, system) -> Result<()>` to call `self.parse_all()?` before switching `self.system`, so every worksheet is read under the old system and then carries typed values. Do nothing when the system is unchanged. Update the doc and the bindings' call sites (P10/P11). Pin it in rust/tests/excel/workbook.rs with the two-sheet repro: the unparsed sheet's date must be identical after the switch.

findings.issue: `CellStyle` derives `Default`, so `CellStyle::default().number_format` is the empty string. The field is documented as 'the format code, `General` for none', and the workbook's own default xf resolves to `"General"`. VERIFIED: `*styles.style(StyleId::DEFAULT).unwrap() == CellStyle::default()` is false. `StyleSheet::find`/`intern` on a default-derived style would therefore miss the default xf. `number_format_id("")` would declare a new custom `numFmt` with an empty `formatCode`. `Splice::temporal` only avoids this because it overwrites the field. The test `a_style_stating_nothing_is_what_a_cell_stating_no_style_shows` never checks the field.
findings.fix: Replace the derive with `impl Default for CellStyle` using `number_format: SmolStr::new_static("General")` and the other fields' defaults. Add `assert_eq!(CellStyle::default().number_format, "General")` and equality with `Workbook::new().style_sheet()?.style(StyleId::DEFAULT)` to rust/tests/excel/style.rs.

findings.issue: The module doc says the styles and the shared strings are written again 'only by appending, so every index a cell states keeps naming what it named'. That is true for styles. It is false for the shared strings: `SharedStringTable::write` regenerates the whole `sst`. VERIFIED (probe G): a dirty sheet adding one string turns an existing rich item `<si><r><t>be</t></r><r><t>ta</t></r></si>` into `<si><t xml:space="preserve">beta</t></si>`, and `count` counts only the rewritten sheets' references (2, against 3 or more in the package). The agent listed this as P2 work, but the shipped rustdoc claims the opposite.
findings.fix: Until P2's `package::rewrite`-based sst append lands, reword the sentence: styles are appended to, the shared strings are regenerated from their text (rich runs and phonetic text of existing items are flattened, `count` covers written sheets only). Keep index positions as the stated invariant.

findings.issue: `temporal_format(dtype)` restates the rule `DateSystem::serial_of` (cell.rs:301-331) applies per value: Date32/64 give Date; a naive DateTime64 gives DateTime for seconds and DateTimeFraction otherwise; Time32/64 give Time; Duration gives Duration. That is two owners of one fact. If they drift, `SheetXml` fails at the first temporal row with 'expected a style for the {format} format among the ones interned', or a column is styled under a format the value does not spell. AGENTS §1: one owner per fact.
findings.fix: Put the mapping in one place, for example `NumberFormat::of_temporal(id_or_dtype, unit, naive) -> Option<Self>` in styles.rs, and have both `serial_of` and `temporal_formats` call it. Add a test iterating one value per temporal leaf that asserts `serial_of(value).1 == temporal_format(value.dtype())`.

findings.issue: The general append path shipped in this phase is never executed by any test: `write_font`, `write_fill` (including `Fill::Gradient` raw carry), `write_border`, `write_color`, the alignment and protection halves of `write_xf`, and `intern` for a style whose font, fill or border are new. The only caller in P1b is `Splice::temporal`, which reuses font, fill and border 0. The agent recorded this as 'P3 should pin it'. AGENTS requires the surface a phase writes to be pinned, with the round trip the design asks for ('append-only splice writer with count patches').
findings.fix: Add a `#[cfg(feature = "internals")] pub mod internals` forwarder in styles.rs that exposes `intern` and `to_part`, and re-run `python scripts/generate_internals.py` followed by `--check`. Pin in rust/tests/excel/styles.rs `mod internal`: intern styles with bold and italic, underline, theme, indexed and rgb colours with tint, pattern and gradient fills, per-edge borders with diagonals, non-default alignment and protection, and `quote_prefix`. Then `to_part`, `StyleSheet::from_xml`, and assert `style(id)` equality with the input, unchanged pre-existing entries, and correct patched `count`s. Also cover a part that lacks each list. If the forwarder is deferred, delete the untested writers from P1b rather than carry them.

findings.issue: Design §3.2 says `StyleSheet` reads every `cellXfs` fact including `pivotButton` and the `apply*` flags. `read_xf` reads neither, and `Xf` and `CellStyle` hold no field for them. `StyleSheet::find` (content equality over resolved `CellStyle`s) can therefore treat an xf carrying `pivotButton="1"` or `applyX="0"` as identical to a plain one. `Splice::temporal` could reuse it for a temporal cell, and P3's derived xfs would silently drop the flag.
findings.fix: Add private `pivot_button: bool` and the apply flags to `Xf`, read them in `read_xf` (`flag()`), write them in `write_xf`, and either compare them in `find` or exclude an xf that has `pivotButton` from `find`. Pin with a carried xf `pivotButton="1"` that must not be reused as a temporal style.

findings.issue: `styles_revision` and `styles_saved` are never incremented anywhere: `grep` shows only initialisation, the `is_dirty` comparison, `write_preserving`'s `styles_dirty` and `Snapshot`. `styles_dirty` is therefore always false, and `held_styles = any_dirty || styles_dirty`, `(None, Some(held)) if styles_dirty || styles_created` and the `is_dirty` term are dead branches. The counter pair replaced the design's `styles_dirty: bool` with reasoning ('rebase needs to tell later edits apart') that only matters once something moves it, which is P3. This is speculative state with no pin.
findings.fix: Either delete `styles_revision`, `styles_saved`, `Snapshot::styles` and the dead branches until P3 introduces `set_style`, or keep them and add the one pin that gives them meaning in this phase. If kept, the `is_dirty` doc must not imply styles can be dirty today.

findings.issue: `set_date_system` silently moves every date of every sheet that was not parsed. Unparsed sheets are copied raw with their old serials, while the rewritten workbook part states the new epoch. `parse()` (line 831) also reads a not-yet-parsed sheet under the new `self.system`, so the same file gives different dates depending on which sheets were read first. Verified: a two-sheet package with a Date32 cell (19_723) on each sheet, `set_date_system(Year1904)` with nothing parsed, save, reopen: both cells read 21_185 (+1462 days). Parsed sheets convert correctly, so the result depends on read order. The behaviour existed before P1b, but the design lists the date system under `documents_dirty` and P1b now owns the dirty rule and the workbook-part rewrite.
findings.fix: Keep every sheet's serials meaningful. In `parse()` call `Sheet::from_rows(..)` with `self.stated_system`, then `if self.system != self.stated_system { sheet.set_date_system(self.system) }`; this bumps the revision, so the sheet is dirty and rewritten under the new epoch. In `write_preserving`, when `self.system != self.stated_system`, treat every worksheet slot as dirty and get it with `self.parsed(at)?` (lazy parse under the stated system). Alternatively make `set_date_system` return `Result<()>` and call `parse_all()` before switching; both bindings already return `Result`. Pin: two sheets, only one parsed, switch to 1904, save, and both dates keep their calendar day.

findings.issue: Fragments written into `xl/workbook.xml` (and, in styles.rs:922-939, into `xl/styles.xml`) ignore the document's element prefix and where `xmlns:r` is bound, although package.rs:485 claims a part that prefixes its elements is edited alike. The regenerated `<sheet ... r:id=..>` (line 1351), the inserted `<calcPr fullCalcOnLoad="1"/>` (line 1374) and the appended `<numFmt>`/`<xf>` are all unprefixed. Verified with an Open XML SDK style workbook part (`<x:workbook xmlns:x=..>`, `xmlns:r` declared on each `<x:sheet>`): a rename gives `<x:sheets><sheet .. r:id=..>` with no binding for `r`. openpyxl fails with `ParseError: unbound prefix` and LibreOffice reports `source file could not be loaded`. A plain cell edit on the same package inserts `<calcPr>` in no namespace under the prefixed root. The `x:`-prefixed styles part likewise gets an unprefixed `<xf>` inside `<x:cellXfs>`. Any dirty save now triggers the `calcPr` insertion, so the trigger is wider than the sheet-list case.
findings.fix: Read the prefix of the `sheets` / `styleSheet` element (a small `package::element_prefix(bytes, local_name)` pre-scan) and render every fragment with it. Emit `xmlns:r="<relationships namespace>"` on each generated `<sheet>`, which is always valid, or reuse the prefix bound at the root. Apply the same prefix to the `calcPr`/`workbookPr` insertions and to the styles fragments. Add a test with an `x:`-prefixed workbook part that binds `xmlns:r` on `<x:sheet>`: rename, add a sheet, edit a cell, then parse the output namespace-aware.

findings.issue: Regression from the pre-P1b writer. `PartWriter::cell` refuses `own >= table.len()` even for `StyleId::DEFAULT`. A styles part with no `cellXfs` (or an empty one, which the schema allows) has `len() == 0`, so every cell that states no `s` is refused: `expected a style the workbook's 0 cell formats hold, got index 0` at `Data!A1`. Verified with a styles part holding only `<fonts>` and with `<cellXfs count="0"/>`; both saves fail, and the old writer saved them. The record path is worse. `Splice::temporal` (styles.rs:1473) interns the first temporal xf as index 0 in the empty table, which equals `StyleId::DEFAULT`. The date cell is written with no `s`, and every other unstyled cell then resolves to xf 0. Verified through `overwrite_arrow_reader`: styles.xml becomes `<cellXfs count="1"><xf numFmtId="164" ..>` and `A2 = 187.23` (no `s`) renders as a date.
findings.fix: Treat `StyleId::DEFAULT` as always valid in `write_xml` (only refuse `own != DEFAULT && own >= len`). In `StyleSheet::from_xml`, when the part lists no `cellXfs` entry, seed an implicit default `Xf` at index 0 and leave it past `read.xfs`, so `to_part` writes it and interned styles start at 1. Pins: cellXfs-less package saved through `Workbook` (a cell with no style, then a date cell) and through the record path (the number cell keeps the default style).

findings.issue: `rebase` accepts a package older than one already adopted, and `write_preserving` silently skips a clean slot whose part is not in the source (copy loop at line 1278 only walks `members`). Verified: `p1 = into_package(); add_sheet("Late")+edit; p2 = into_package(); rebase(p2); rebase(p1)` (the order two overlapping saves in the service can finish in). The stale adopt replaces the source with p1's archive, but slot `Late` keeps the part p2 gave it and counts as clean. The next `into_bytes()` returns Ok with `<sheet name="Late" r:id=..>` and no `xl/worksheets/sheet4.xml`, and reading that sheet gives `Absent workbook part xl/worksheets/sheet4.xml`. A corrupt package is produced with no error.
findings.fix: Make the check two-part. (1) Stamp each `Snapshot` with a per-workbook increasing sequence taken in `into_package`; `rebase` refuses `snapshot.sequence <= self.rebased` with `Error::Conflict` (expected a package newer than the last adopted). (2) In `write_preserving`, for every non-dirty slot with `Some(part)`, return `Error::absent("workbook part", part)` when `!held(part)`, so a dangling sheet becomes a named refusal. Pin both with the sequence above.

findings.issue: `rewrite` treats end of input inside an open element as success. A workbook part, relationships part or content-types part cut before its root end tag makes every `before_end` fragment and pending insertion silently not fire. Fuzzed cases: truncated `xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels` followed by `add_sheet` gives a workbook part naming `r:id="rId7"` with no such relationship; a truncated `xl/workbook.xml` loses the added sheet. The package is internally inconsistent and nothing reports it.
findings.fix: Track `open` (already kept) and at `Event::Eof` return `codec_error(position, "unclosed element <name>")` if it is non-empty. Test one truncated part per rewritten document.

findings.issue: Input-reachable integer overflow panics; in release they wrap silently. All verified in a debug build: `sheetId="4294967295"` plus a `<sheet>` stating no id panics at `Workbook::open` (workbook.rs:483 `last_sheet_id += 1`); after any tab has that id, `add_sheet` panics at workbook.rs:776. A relationship `Id="rId18446744073709551615"` then any save that adds a sheet panics in `Relationships::next_id` (package.rs:285-290). A member named `xl/worksheets/sheet18446744073709551615.xml` panics in `write_preserving` (workbook.rs:1107-1116, `next_number`). A declared `numFmtId="4294967295"` plus any new number format panics at styles.rs:811 (`.max(163) + 1`); in release the new id wraps to 0 and would redeclare General.
findings.fix: Use `checked_add` at all five sites. On overflow return `Error::InvalidRecord` naming the part, or pick the smallest unused id. In `number_format_id` refuse when no id above the highest one in use is left.

findings.issue: The new `numFmtId` is `max(163, highest declared) + 1`. It ignores ids that `cellXfs` (and `cellStyleXfs`) name but the part never declares. An xf naming undeclared id 169 reads as General, and the first appended format takes id 169, so existing cells silently change format after the save. Reproduced by fuzz: a `numFmt` entry with an unreadable id was dropped from `codes`, and cell `Data!C3` read General before the save and Date after it. Likewise a raw-copied sheet stating `s` past `cellXfs` is read as DEFAULT but keeps its `s`, and starts naming the first appended xf. This breaks the stated 'every index keeps naming what it named' invariant for dangling references.
findings.fix: Compute the new id as `max(163, declared ids, every numFmtId any xf names) + 1`; keep the used-id maximum from the xf scan in `from_xml`. For dangling `s`, either accept the documented limit or refuse growth when a stored `s` is out of range.

findings.issue: The outside-implementation check never reads what the new append-only splice writer produced. The openpyxl edit test writes only text, so `styles.xml` is copied untouched. The appended `numFmt`, `xf` and patched counts (the riskiest new code in the phase) are checked only by this crate's own reader. I verified by hand that openpyxl and LibreOffice accept them: a workbook that openpyxl wrote, with a bold header and a percent cell, edited with date, datetime-ms, time and duration cells, gives `yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss.000`, `h:mm:ss` and `[h]:mm:ss` numFmts, bold and `0.00%` kept. This is not pinned.
findings.fix: In `edits_the_styled_workbook_the_external_writer_produced_keeping_its_styles` also set a datetime (ms) cell, a time cell and a duration cell, and extend `read_edited_with_openpyxl` to assert each cell's `number_format` and Python type alongside the bold/percent assertions.

fixed.summary:
I checked all 16 findings against the code. 15 are fixed, each with a test that fails on the old code. Finding 12 is fixed in its first half only; its second half is explained in deviations. The phase smoke, `cargo fmt --all`, both clippy lanes and the openpyxl exchange all pass. Every build ran in `/dev/shm/p1b-target` because the shared disk is full (see open items).

Per finding:
1 and 11 (a styles part with no `cellXfs`): fixed. When a list is empty, `StyleSheet::from_xml` now puts the default xf, font, fill (`none` plus `gray125`) and border at index 0, after what it read. So the first interned style is index 1 or later, and a save writes the defaults first. `PartWriter::cell` no longer refuses `StyleId::DEFAULT`. Tests cover a workbook save for both missing and `count="0"` lists, and the record path (a Date32 plus Float64 row).
2 and 9 (date system): fixed without changing the signature, because both bindings call `set_date_system` as a statement and it must stay infallible. `parse()` reads a part under the stated system, then converts to the current one. When the system changed, `write_preserving` marks every worksheet dirty and parses it. `media::source` reads raw parts under the stated system. Test: nothing, one or both sheets parsed before the switch; every date keeps its day.
3: `CellStyle` now has a hand-written `Default` whose number format is "General". It equals the default style of `Workbook::new()`.
4: the rustdoc sentence now describes how shared strings are really rewritten.
5: new `NumberFormat::of_temporal(id, unit, naive)` (pub(crate)) is the one rule. `DateSystem::serial_of` and the writer's `temporal_format` both call it. A new test writes one column per temporal leaf and unit.
6: added `excel::styles::internals::{from_xml, intern, to_part}` and regenerated `lib.rs`. Round-trip tests cover every font, fill (including gradient), border, alignment, protection and colour fact, deduplication, unchanged earlier entries and patched counts. They run over the rich part and over a part lacking every list.
7: `Xf` now holds `pivot_button` and the six `apply` flags, and `write_xf` writes them. `find` only reuses an xf that shows no pivot button and states no `apply` flag false.
8: removed `styles_revision`, `styles_saved`, `Snapshot::styles` and the branches that could never run.
10: fragments written by `rewrite` now take the prefix of the element they go into. The new `package::scope_of` finds the prefix bound to the relationships namespace; when none is bound, each generated `<sheet>` declares `xmlns:r` itself. Tests parse the output with namespaces, including the case where `sheets` rebinds `r` to another namespace.
12: `Snapshot::sequence` plus `Workbook::adopted`. `rebase` refuses a package built before the last one adopted with `Error::Conflict`; `write_into` counts as an adoption.
13: `rewrite` refuses a part that ends inside an open element. One test covers each rewritten document.
14: the five overflow points no longer panic. A `sheetId` or worksheet part number that would overflow takes the lowest free number instead. A relationship id or `numFmtId` that would overflow gives a named refusal.
15: new format codes take an id past every id the styles part mentions, including ids that `xf` and `dxf` entries use without declaring. A sheet copied unchanged whose `s` points past the list is a limit I documented rather than tracked.
16: the openpyxl edit now also writes a datetime to the millisecond, a time and a duration. Both sides assert each cell's format and type.

No public item was added or removed. Behaviour changed for `CellStyle::default()`, `Workbook::set_date_system`, `Workbook::rebase` (new refusal) and `StyleSheet::len` (now 1 for a part with no cell format).

deviations: Finding 12, second half (refuse a clean slot whose part the source lacks): not done. After the sequence check, the stale-rebase case can no longer happen. The only other way to reach it is opening a package whose sheet relationship already points at a missing member (pinned by rust/tests/excel/package.rs a_sheet_relationship_naming_a_missing_member_is_refused_naming_the_part). Carrying that dangling reference unchanged keeps the design's rule that a save changes only what was edited; refusing would block every save of such a file.

Findings 2 and 9: fixed through the parse path (read under the stated system, then convert; every worksheet rewritten when the system changed) rather than making set_date_system return Result. The Python and Node bindings call it as a statement, so a Result return would raise unused_must_use and break the bindings' clippy in files outside my set.

Finding 7: the xf flags are read and written, but find does not compare them. It skips any xf with pivotButton or an apply flag stated false. This never reuses a wrong entry; a LibreOffice file, which writes apply*='false', gets a duplicate temporal xf appended instead.

Findings 1 and 11 extend beyond cellXfs: fonts and borders are seeded with a default, and fills with none plus gray125, whenever their list is empty. Otherwise an appended entry would take index 0, which existing xfs already resolve to the default.

Finding 15: the new-id maximum also counts dxf numFmt ids, the id space Excel shares. As a result, the existing pin a_save_appends_to_the_styles_and_carries_everything_the_model_does_not_read moved from id 165 to 171 (the rich part's dxf declares 170); the test comment says why.
Finding 10: the prefix fix is generic in package::rewrite, so it also covers prefixed .rels and [Content_Types].xml parts, not only workbook.xml and styles.xml.
Also fixed while doing finding 2: media::source now reads raw sheet parts under the stated date system (new pub(crate) Workbook::stated_date_system).
open: The shared disk is full: / shows 195M free, and the shared target/debug holds about 23G (14G of it incremental caches). My first build failed with ENOSPC. The auto-mode classifier denied deleting incremental caches older than 2h, so I did not delete anything shared. Every build in this round ran in /dev/shm/p1b-target (tmpfs, now 6.6G of the machine's 15G RAM). I left it warm for the next step; it is safe to rm -rf when no longer needed. The next agent needs either that CARGO_TARGET_DIR or someone to free the shared target (a decision for the user).

For P3, which is not reached in P1b: a fills list holding exactly one entry is not padded to Excel's reserved [none, gray125]. A fill interned by set_style would take index 1, which Excel reads as gray125. P1b's temporal xfs always reuse fill 0.
Documented limit, not fixed: a sheet copied unchanged whose `s` points past cellXfs will point at whatever xf a later save appends at that index. Parsed and rewritten sheets are unaffected.
Cost of the date-system fix: after set_date_system, the next save parses and rewrites every worksheet. There is no iobase_calls pin for that path yet.
The shared-strings append that keeps rich runs and phonetic text is still P2; the rustdoc now states the current regeneration behaviour.
The .api-inventory.txt and .api-bindings.txt were not touched; this round adds no public name.
